messages:
Olivia Chen: incoming ticket from Acme Corp — users can't finish OAuth login for GitHub and Google. After consent they land on our callback and see a 400 with 'state_mismatch'. Happening for multiple users and both providers. Customer gave callback: https://acme.app/auth/callback (no trailing slash). They also said sometimes it worked, sometimes it fails. Escalating.

Maria Gomez: thanks. any logs or a sample callback URL we can look at (please strip tokens)? also did they use a custom domain or proxy in front of app?

Olivia Chen: customer confirmed they use CloudFront in front of the app. Provided example callback URL (sanitized):
https://acme.app/auth/callback?state=Z3Vlc3QxMjM&code=Spl1tCodE&provider=github
they say server returns 400 and shows 'state_mismatch'.

Sam Patel: quick checklist — 1) redirect_uri exact match in provider app (trailing slash / query params), 2) state param being lost/rewritten by proxy, 3) session cookie not set (so code_verifier/state stored server-side missing), 4) double-URL-encoding of redirect_uri on our side, 5) PKCE code_verifier mismatch if code_verifier wasn't saved. CloudFront can strip cookies or rewrite querystring depending on behavior.

Sam Patel: can we reproduce quickly? try curl to our callback with the state they sent and a dummy session cookie to see how we handle validation. Example reproduce: 

curl -i -L 
  'https://redwood-internal.test/auth/callback?state=Z3Vlc3QxMjM&code=dummycode&provider=github' 
  -H 'Cookie: session=eyJ...'

If server responds with 400 show logs: we should see something like:

[auth] WARN 2026-02-18T14:12:02Z state_mismatch expected=Y7x4N got=Z3Vlc3QxMjM session_id=missing cookie_present=false

Sam Patel: note that if session_id is missing it's usually cookie domain/path/SameSite issue or proxy stripping Set-Cookie on initial /login redirect. PKCE flows store code_verifier in session between /login and /callback — no session means mismatch.

Maria Gomez: customer said sometimes it works which smells like a caching layer or sticky session problem at CloudFront / LB. If some requests hit instance A (with session) and callback lands on instance B (no session), you'll see intermittent state_mismatch.

Derek Huang: assigning to eng-auth oncall to validate sticky sessions and cookie behavior. @Sam can you drop the auth handler debug logs to the thread? I want to see Set-Cookie on the /login -> response and the /callback incoming request headers.

Sam Patel: pasted sample debug (sanitized):

=== request to /login ===
Host: acme.app
Set-Cookie: session=abc123; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
Location: https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?...&state=Y7x4N

=== request to /callback (when failing) ===
GET /auth/callback?state=Z3Vlc3QxMjM&code=Spl1tCodE
Cookie:   
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (CloudFront)

Server log: state_mismatch expected=Y7x4N got=Z3Vlc3QxMjM session_id=missing

Sam Patel: oh — SameSite=Lax will block cookies in some cross-site scenarios if the redirect chain includes cross-site navigations or if the provider uses POST/redirect. For strict PKCE/OAuth we recommend SameSite=None; Secure. CloudFront might also be caching the /login redirect response (removing Set-Cookie) if cache policy includes Set-Cookie not forwarded. That would cause intermittent successes.

Maria Gomez: immediate action items for support to send to customer: 1) check provider app redirect_uri exactly matches registered value (including trailing slash), 2) ensure our domain sets SameSite=None and Secure on session cookies for cross-site OAuth flows, 3) confirm CloudFront cache behavior forwards cookies and does not cache the /login response, 4) share full request/response headers for a failing attempt (we'll redact tokens).

Olivia Chen: I asked customer to capture a failing network trace and to confirm if they see Set-Cookie on the /login response. Also asked them to try a temporary test by disabling CloudFront (point DNS directly) to confirm.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-3421 updated — added triage notes. Customer asked for ETA.

Derek Huang: long-term fixes for eng-auth: (a) make our cookie SameSite=None for OAuth flows, (b) instrument and log redirect_uri_registered boolean and more context on state/code mismatch errors (include provider, expected_state, got_state masked), (c) detect when Set-Cookie is absent on /login and surface a clearer diagnostic to the user, (d) add a doc page on common redirect_uri/PKCE/state pitfalls (trailing slash, proxy caching).

Sam Patel: also watch out for double-encoding of redirect_uri in provider config — e.g., registering https%3A%2F%2Facme.app%2Fauth%2Fcallback vs https://acme.app/auth/callback will not match. GitHub typically requires exact match. Google sometimes allows multiple redirect URIs but still exact match per entry.

Maria Gomez: customer did one test after disabling caching and said OAuth flow completed successfully. So root cause = CloudFront caching the login redirect or stripping Set-Cookie. Customer will change cache behavior to forward cookies and disable caching on /login.

Olivia Chen: closing loop with customer and asked them to re-open if they see it again. Created internal ticket on eng-auth: https://redwood.internal/issue/RED-9842 (private) to update cookie defaults and add better logging.

Derek Huang: I'll follow up tomorrow to check progress on RED-9842. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
